claims.behaviour: `item-provider` answers only attribute id `item` and reads no params (a request with extra params is still served, following the `SimpleAttributeProvider` matching rules, C-0194/C-0195). It registers two loaders: one in the generic value format (`ValueFormat` id `value`) and one in format `any`. A request for `item:any` gets the raw-object loader, a request for `item:value` the extended-value loader; for any other requested format the extended-value loader (registered first) is chosen.

For `item` in the `value` format, the value of every row is the row's own `ItemIdentity` (the identity itself, not the resolved object), for every item type, including items that do not exist or the user cannot see; the loader resolves nothing. Its caching strategy is `MAY`.

For `item:any`, the value is the object the item resolves to for the attribute context (`ItemAttributeContext.getItem(Object.class)`): for example the Jira `Issue` for an issue, the `Project`, `ApplicationUser`, `Folder`, `GenericItem` and so on. An item that does not resolve (missing, invisible, or of a type whose app is absent) gives the undefined value. This loader supports every item type and its caching strategy is `SHOULD_NOT` (values are never kept in the value cache).

`displayable-provider` answers only attribute id `displayable` (format text) and reads no params. Every value is a localized text built with the attribute context's i18n helper (`AttributeContext.getI18n()`), so every part declares the `USER_LOCALE` context dependency. Items of types not listed in the following claims get the undefined value.

For an issue row with a key the value is `s.ext.it.issue.displayable` (`issue {0} ({1})`) with the issue key and the summary shortened to at most 30 characters the way Commons Lang `StringUtils.abbreviate(s, 30)` does (a longer summary becomes its first 27 characters plus `...`). For an issue without a key (a new issue being created) it is `s.ext.it.new-issue.displayable` (`a new issue ({0})`) with the shortened summary. The issue comes from the row's `item` attribute; for the new-issue row (`CoreIdentities.NEW_ISSUE`) whose `item` is not an `Issue`, the issue object carried by the row itself is used. An issue row whose issue cannot be obtained gets the undefined value. The value depends on the `item` attribute.
An issue whose summary is null gives the text with the summary argument null, which Jira's i18n formatting shows as the text `null` (e.g. `issue ABC-1 (null)`).

For a folder row the value is `s.ext.it.folder.displayable` (`folder {0}`). For a folder with a string item id (a generated folder) the argument is the folder name translated as an i18n key with the context's i18n helper (an unknown key comes back as is); for a folder with a long id it is the folder name unchanged. The folder comes from the row's `item` attribute, or for the new-folder row (`CoreIdentities.NEW_FOLDER`) from the row itself; otherwise the value is undefined.
Every generator item gets `s.ext.it.generator.displayable` (`a generator`) and every effector item `s.ext.it.effector.displayable` (`an effector`), whether or not the generator or effector exists.

For a row whose item type is a generic item type (memos, planning tasks and any other item type registered as a generic item type in `extension-service`) the value is the item type module's `displayable` text (its descriptor's configured displayable i18n text) formatted with the generic item's name. If the item type has no descriptor, or the generic item cannot be obtained (from the `item` attribute, or for long id `Long.MAX_VALUE` from the row itself), the value is undefined. A null text gives the undefined value.

For resolved items of the following types the value is the i18n key (whose literal name contains the `+` signs) with one argument: project `s.ext.it.+project+.displayable` (`project {0}`, the project name); component `s.ext.it.+component+.displayable` (`component {0}`, its name); version `s.ext.it.+version+.displayable` (`version {0}`, its name); issue type `s.ext.it.+issuetype+.displayable` (`issue type {0}`, the translated name); status, resolution and priority `s.ext.it.+status+.displayable`, `s.ext.it.+resolution+.displayable`, `s.ext.it.+priority+.displayable` (`status {0}`, `resolution {0}`, `priority {0}`, the raw untranslated name); user `s.ext.it.+user+.displayable` (`user {0}`, the display name); group `s.ext.it.+group+.displayable` (`group {0}`); label `s.ext.it.+label+.displayable` (`label {0}`); custom field option `s.ext.it.+cfoption+.displayable` (`option {0}`, the option value, or `Parent - Child` for a child option as `JiraFunc.OPTION_NAME`, C-0879); structure `s.ext.it.+structure+.displayable` (`structure {0}`); sprint `s.ext.it.+sprint+.displayable` (`sprint {0}`, the raw sprint name); Tempo account `s.ext.it.+tempo-account+.displayable` (`account {0}`, its name); version name `s.ext.it.+version-name+.displayable` (`version name {0}`); loop marker `s.ext.it.+loopmarker+.displayable` (`a loop marker`, no argument used). An item of these types that does not resolve gets the undefined value.

`number-sum-provider` answers only attribute id `sum`. Params read: `attribute` (the summed attribute, a nested spec object `{id, format, params}` read as `SpecParams.getAttributeParameter`, C-0961), `distinct` (boolean, default false), `type` (string: `preceding` selects a running total; any other value, or none, is the reduction strategy type of `ReductionStrategy`, default `subtree`), and with `distinct` also `rowBased` (boolean, default false). Any other param (for example `levels` and `baseLevel`) is passed along unchanged in the spec to the sum loaders and the duplicate-counting attribute.

The sum's value format is chosen in this order: (1) if the requested format is `number` or `duration`, that format is used and `attribute` is read expecting it (its stored `format` must be absent, the same, or `any`); (2) otherwise, if `attribute` carries a stored standard format that is `number` or `duration`, that format is used; (3) otherwise a `number` sum is tried, reading `attribute` as `number`, which succeeds only when its stored format is `any` (or absent/`number`). Example: `sum:text` over `{id: votes, format: number}` is served as a number sum; over `{id: x, format: duration}` as a duration sum.

The provider declines (returns no loader) when the id is not `sum`, when `attribute` is missing or not an object, when its stored format conflicts with the format chosen above, or, for a requested format other than `number`/`duration`, when `attribute` has no stored format or a stored format other than `number`, `duration` or `any`. So a dependent stored as `text` (e.g. `{id: x, format: text}`) is not summed.

Without `distinct` and with a `type` other than `preceding`, a duration sum totals the summed attribute's `Long` values as `LongSumLoader` does (C-0180/C-0181) and a number sum as `NumberSumLoader` does (C-0189 to C-0191), aggregating over the forest with the reduction strategy named by `type` (`subtree` default: the row's own value plus its sub-rows; `children`, `leaves`, `strict` as in C-0267 to C-0270). Undefined values are skipped; a sum with no defined contribution is undefined. The sum depends only on the summed attribute.

With `type` = `preceding` (and no `distinct`) the value of each row is a running total of the summed attribute over the rows that precede it in forest order plus the row itself, as `ScanningLongSumLoader` (duration, C-0192) or `ScanningNumberSumLoader` (number, C-0193) computes it.

With `distinct` = true each item is counted once within what a row totals: the value is the non-distinct sum (the same spec without `distinct` and `rowBased`) minus, for every item that occurs k > 1 times among the counted rows, (k - 1) times that item's value. Only items that occur more than once in the whole forest are considered. Example: row A (own 5) with children B (3), C (2) and B again gives 13 without distinct and 10 with distinct. With `type` = `strict` the row's own item is counted one time fewer (strict sums exclude the row itself). Duration and number variants behave alike (numbers keep their accumulated `Number` type).

A distinct sum depends on the non-distinct sum spec (same id, format and params minus `distinct` and `rowBased`) and on the `-non-unique-items` attribute (format `counts`) carrying the traversal params `type`, `levels` and `baseLevel` of the request (a `type` of `strict` or `subtree` is dropped), which `non-unique-items-provider` serves. The duplicated items' values are, by default, each item's own value of the summed attribute loaded separately for that item; when `rowBased` is true, or when the summed attribute is not an item-based attribute, they are taken instead from an extra `-non-unique-items` dependency in format `values` with the summed attribute as its `attribute` param (the values shown in the rows). The second case also logs at INFO `attempt to use SUM with a row-based attribute - forcing rowBased=true for the sum of <spec>`.

For a distinct sum, when the non-distinct total is an error or undefined that same value is returned unchanged; when loading the duplicated items' values fails, the value is the error value and a warning `-- item loader failed, there may be missing values` is logged (throttled per spec). An item whose value is undefined is not subtracted.

`error-provider` answers only attribute id `value-expand`, in format `json` (a JSON object), and needs param `attribute`: a nested spec `{id, format, params}` whose `format` names a standard value format (read as `SpecParams.getAttributeParameter` with no expected format, C-0961). Without `attribute`, or when it has no format or a non-standard one, the spec is declined. The value depends only on that inner attribute.

For each row the value is a one-key JSON object built from the inner attribute's value: an error value gives `{"error": <code>}` where code is the formula error code carried by the value (see `expr-attribute`), or -1 when the error carries none; any other undefined value (plain undefined, absent, inaccessible) gives `{"undefined": true}`; a defined value v gives `{"value": v}`. The result itself is always defined.

`main-provider` answers attribute ids `summary` (text), `description` (html, and a separate text variant when `description` is requested in format `text`), `extended-summary` (html) and `url` (text). It reads no params. Item types not listed below get the undefined value.

`summary` per item type: issue: its summary; project: its name; version: its name; label: the label; status: its name translated for the context locale; issue type: its translated name; resolution and priority: the raw (untranslated) name; component: its name; custom field option: the option value (or `Parent - Child`, C-0879); group: its name; structure: its name; version name: the name. An item that does not resolve gets the undefined value, and a null name gives the undefined value.

`summary` of a folder: for a folder with a string item id (generated folder), a name starting with `/` is returned without that first character, and any other name is treated as an i18n key and translated for the Jira logged-in user; for a folder with a long id the name is returned unchanged; an unresolved folder gives the undefined value. This part declares `USER_LOCALE` and caching strategy `MAY`.
`summary` of a user is the user's display name; for an inactive user it is `s.ext.it.user.summary.inactive` (`{0} (Inactive)`) with the display name, translated for the Jira logged-in user.

`summary` of a sprint is the sprint name formatted for the current Structure user by `gh-integration` (board name and state decoration, C-2246); with Jira Software absent sprint items do not resolve and get the undefined value. `summary` of a Tempo account is `s.ext.gen.grouper.tempo.accounts.account.summary` (`{0} {1}`) with the account name and, for an account that is not open, `(` + the translated status (`s.tempo.accounts.status.closed` `Closed` or `s.tempo.accounts.status.archived` `Archived`) + `)`; an open account gives the name followed by one space (as the original does).

`summary` of a Service Management request type is its name, only while the Service Management app is accessible (C-2316; otherwise undefined); of a generic item (any generic item type, memos and planning tasks included) its name; of an Assets (Insight) object its label (undefined when Assets is absent and the object does not resolve).

`description` (html): for a project or version, its description HTML-escaped; an empty or null description gives the undefined value. For a sprint, its goal HTML-escaped (undefined when null). For a generic item of a generic item type other than memo and planning task (whose descriptions come from other providers), its description rendered by Jira's renderer `atlassian-wiki-renderer` (looked up from `RendererManager` once when the provider is created, rendered with no issue context) or, if Jira has no such renderer, HTML-escaped; an empty result gives the undefined value.

`description` in format `text`: a sprint's goal and a version's description as plain text (as `sprint-parameters-provider` and `version-parameters-provider` serve them), and for a generic item of a type other than memo and planning task its raw description (empty or null gives the undefined value). Projects have no text description from this provider.

`extended-summary` (html) is served for generator and effector items: the value is always defined, `CONTENT` for generators and `CONTENT` for effectors, with CONTENT `?` when nothing could be produced. The loader declares the `TRAIL` context dependency; for a sub-structure inserter generator it adds the inserted structure to the trail, so a change of that structure invalidates the value.

For a resolved generator with a module descriptor, or an effector instance whose module (descriptor and effector) is installed, CONTENT is the module's `summary` Velocity resource rendered with the module's summary parameters and trimmed (leading and trailing whitespace and ` `/` `/` ` removed). Each string parameter is shown as `VALUE` (HTML-escaped), a collection as such spans joined by `, `, a blank string or empty collection as `none specified` (`s.ext.aut.none-specified`); the template also gets `i18n`, `rawParameters` and `noneSpecified`. If the rendered summary is blank, the module label is used, else its key (with a warning). Exceptions while the module adds its parameters are logged and ignored. An effector instance with a non-blank `effectorName` parameter shows that name HTML-escaped instead.

An unresolvable generator, or one without a descriptor, gets `s.ext.gen.summary.unknown` (`Unknown generator {0}`) with `MODULEKEY`, the module key the generator manager records for that generator id (`?` if none), in the current user's locale. An effector whose module is not installed gets `s.ext.eff.summary.unknown` (`Unknown effector {0}`) with the instance's module key in that span; when the effector instance itself does not resolve, the item id's simplified text is shown in place of the module key.

`url` (text): issue and project: `<base URL>/browse/<KEY>`; user: `<base URL>/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=<username>`; memo and planning task: the board link of `generic-item-type-helper` (C-2687); Assets (Insight) object: `<base URL>/secure/insight/assets/<object key>`. The base URL is the attribute context's base URL. Keys and usernames are HTML-escaped (not URL-encoded); the Assets key is inserted as is. Other item types get the undefined value.

`key-provider` answers only attribute id `key` (format text) and reads no params. Values: issue and project: the Jira key; user: the username (login name, not the key); memo: `MEMO:<id>` and planning task: `PT:<id>` (C-2687); Assets (Insight) object: its object key. Items that do not resolve, and all other item types, get the undefined value.

An issue whose key is null (a new issue not yet created) gives a key value created from null: with Java assertions enabled (as the tests run) this throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled the value is the plain undefined value.

`done-provider` answers only attribute id `done` (format boolean) and reads no params. Only issues get a value; other item types get the undefined value, and an issue that does not resolve is undefined.
By default an issue is done (true) exactly when its status's status category key is `done`; an issue with no status, or a status without a category, is not done (false).
When the dark feature `structure.doneAttribute.byResolution` is true (read once, when the provider is created; default false), an issue is done exactly when it has a resolution, whatever its status.

`editable-provider` answers only attribute id `editable` (format boolean), reads no params, and gives true or false for issues, folders, generators, effectors and generic items; other item types get the undefined value. Every part depends on the viewing user (`USER`), and the folder, generator, effector and generic-item parts also declare `TRAIL`.
An issue is editable when Jira's `IssueManager.isEditable(issue, user)` says so for the attribute context's user; an issue that does not resolve gets the undefined value.

A folder with a long id is editable when the folder exists in `folder-manager` and the current user has `EDIT` on its owning structure (`StructureManager.isAccessible(structureId, PermissionLevel.EDIT)`, false for a folder with no owning structure, C-1025); the owning structure is added to the trail, so permission changes on it invalidate the value. A folder with a string id (generated) or that does not exist gives false.

A generator is editable when its item id is a positive even long (a persistent generator; odd transient ids and ids of 0 or less give false), it resolves through the generator manager, the generator module is configurable (the duplicate-removing filter `filter-inserter-extender-duplicates` is not), and `StructureManager.isGeneratorConfigurationAllowed(owningStructure, user)` is true (C-1026). The owning structure is added to the trail. A resolution failure gives false and is logged at debug level.

An effector item with a long id is editable when the effector instance can be read and `StructureManager.isEffectorConfigurationAllowed(owningStructure, user)` is true; the owning structure is added to the trail. A missing instance or any error reading it gives false (logged at debug level); a string id gives false.

A generic item (any generic item type, e.g. memo or planning task) is editable when the current user has `EDIT` on its owning structure (`StructureManager.isAccessible(owner, EDIT)`; no owner gives false); the owning structure is added to the trail. A generic item that does not resolve gets the undefined value.

`icon-provider` answers attribute id `icon` (html) and the per-field icon attributes `project.icon`, `assignee.icon`, `reporter.icon`, `issuetype.icon`, `priority.icon`, `status.icon` and `run-as-user.icon` (all html). `assignee.icon` and `reporter.icon` also read param `print` (boolean): with `print` = true the printable variant is served, otherwise the normal one. No other params are read.

`icon` of an issue is the HTML of `issue-constant-icon-cache` for the issue's type (C-1690 to C-1693; the empty string when the issue has no type). The issue type is added to the trail, so a change of that type invalidates the value; the value declares `USER_LOCALE`.

`icon` of a project, and `project.icon` of an issue (from the issue's `project` attribute), is `` with the key and name HTML-escaped and the attribute context's base URL. `project.icon` declares no context dependencies; an issue without a project gives the undefined value.

`icon` of a user is the HTML of `user-icon-cache` (C-1694 to C-1696). `icon` of a status, issue type or priority item is the HTML of `issue-constant-icon-cache` and declares `USER_LOCALE`; resolutions get no icon (undefined).

`icon` of a version is an empty span with classes chosen by state: unreleased ``, released `... aui-iconfont-version`, archived and unreleased `... aui-iconfont-version-unreleased s-version-icon-archived`, archived and released `... aui-iconfont-version s-version-icon-archived`.

`icon` of a generator is its module's icon: when the generator module declares an icon class (for a sorter whose `desc` parameter is true, the class declared for key `desc` if any), ``; otherwise its `icon` Velocity resource rendered and trimmed; otherwise the undefined value. `icon` of an effector is `` from the descriptor of the instance's effector module; an uninstalled module gives the undefined value.

`icon` of a generic item: when its parameters hold both `iconClass` and `color` (single values), `` with both values HTML-escaped; otherwise `` with the item type module's icon class; the undefined value when the type declares none or has no descriptor.

`icon` of a Service Management request type is the request-type icon HTML (C-2325), only while the Service Management app is accessible (otherwise undefined). `icon` of an Assets (Insight) object is ``.

Per-field icons are derived from the issue's attributes: `assignee.icon` from `assignee` and `reporter.icon` from `reporter` (normal: `user-icon-cache`; with `print` = true: `user-printable-icon-cache`, C-1697), `run-as-user.icon` from `run-as-user` (`run-as-user-provider`) via `user-icon-cache`, all declaring no context dependencies; `status.icon`, `issuetype.icon` and `priority.icon` from `status`, `type` and `priority` via `issue-constant-icon-cache`, declaring `USER_LOCALE`. When the source attribute is undefined (e.g. unassigned) the icon is undefined.

`issue-field-provider` serves, for issues only and with no params read, Jira objects: `type` (format `issuetype`: the `IssueType`), `priority` (`Priority`), `project` (`Project`), `status` (`Status`), `assignee`, `reporter` and `creator` (format `user`: the `ApplicationUser` of that user key). A null field gives the undefined value. Each defined value adds the object's identity to the trail (`CoreIdentities.issueType`, `priority`, `project`, `status`, `user`), so a change of that object invalidates the value.

It also serves `votes` and `watches` (format number: the issue's vote and watcher counts as `Long`), `id` (format id: the issue id as decimal text), and, derived from the object attributes, `project` in format id (the project id as text, from `project`), `issuetype` in format id (the issue type id, from `type`) and `status` in format id (the status id, from `status`). A request for id `project` or `status` gets the object or the id variant according to the requested format (object variant for any other format). Non-issue items get the undefined value.
An issue whose id is null (a new issue) gets `id` = the text `null` (as the original does).

`issue-field-rendering-provider` turns the requested spec into a Jira field id: id `key` becomes `issuekey`; id `customfield` with param `fieldId` (a number or numeric text) becomes `customfield_<fieldId>` (a missing or non-numeric `fieldId` leaves `customfield`); any other id is the field id itself. The value is always HTML (the spec is served in format html whatever format was requested).

It declines field ids that are not `timespent`, `timeestimate` or `timeoriginalestimate` and are not among Jira's available navigable fields as `jira-configuration-cache` lists them (C-2492). Only issues get values; other item types get the undefined value.

`timespent`, `timeestimate`, `timeoriginalestimate`, and custom fields of the Epic Sum Up time type (`aptis.plugins.epicSumUp:epic-sum-up-custom-field-time`, value converted as `spic-sum-up-integration` does, C-2302), render as Jira's short formatted duration (`JiraDurationUtils.getShortFormattedDuration(seconds, user locale)`), HTML-escaped and trimmed; a null or zero duration gives the empty string. These declare `USER_LOCALE`; the `excel` param has no effect on them.

User fields (system `assignee`, `reporter`, `creator`, and custom fields whose JSON schema type is `user`) are derived from the same spec in format `user` (same id and params) and rendered by `user-field-renderer` with param `view` as the view mode (C-1701, C-1702); they declare `USER`. An empty user field, or a user the renderer gives nothing for, gives the undefined value.

Any other field renders as Jira's issue navigator column does (`ColumnLayoutItem.getHtml` for that field at position 0), trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace and ` `/` `/` `. With param `excel` = true the display params `textOnly`, `readOnly` and `nolink` (all true) are passed, giving plain text without links for spreadsheet export; otherwise no display params. The field is looked up in Jira's `FieldManager` once per attribute context; a field that is not navigable gives no value. A custom field not relevant for the issue (not in its field configuration context) gives the undefined value.

When Jira's rendering throws (any exception or linkage error), the value is the empty string; a warning `error rendering field <name>(<id>) for issue <key>` is logged only the first time per field within an attribute context.

The Service Management request type field (when the app is present and the field is its request type field) renders as `ICON NAME` with the request-type icon HTML (C-2325) and the HTML-escaped name of the issue's request type (loaded by issue id, C-2319); an issue without a request type gives the undefined value.

Navigator-rendered fields declare context dependencies by field: system fields depend on the user (`USER`) when the field is `assignee`, `reporter`, `creator`, `voter`, `watcher` or `lastViewed`, otherwise only on `USER_LOCALE`; they are time-dependent (`USER_TIMEZONE` and `CURRENT_TIME`) when the field is `duedate`, `lastViewed`, `timetracking`, `created`, `updated`, `resolutiondate` or `worklog`. Custom fields whose type key starts with `com.atlassian` depend on `USER` when their type's class name contains `User` or `Group` and are time-dependent when it contains `Date` or `Time`; all other custom fields depend on `USER` and are time-dependent.
For a time-dependent navigator-rendered field whose rendered HTML is empty, the value expires after 1 day (`valueExpires(1, DAYS)`), so it is recomputed at least daily.

If a field id is listed among the available navigable fields but Jira's `FieldManager` then returns no navigable field for it (and it is not a user field), creating the loader fails with a NullPointerException instead of declining (as the original does).

`issue-field-order-provider` serves sort values (format `order`, a `Comparable`) for issues. The field id comes from the spec as in `issue-field-rendering-provider` (`key` becomes `issuekey`; `customfield` with `fieldId` becomes `customfield_<n>`, which it never answers). It answers exactly the field ids listed in the next claims and declines every other id; only `issuetype` declares a context dependency (`USER_LOCALE`). A null value gives the undefined value.

`issuekey`: the tuple (project key, issue number) as a `ComparableTuple`, so ABC-9 sorts before ABC-10; a key Jira cannot parse gives the empty tuple `ComparableTuple.NIL` (sorts first). `issuetype`: the issue type name translated for the user's locale. `status`: the status's sequence. `resolution`: the resolution's sequence, `Long.MIN_VALUE` for an unresolved issue (so unresolved sorts first). `priority`: the negated priority sequence (so the highest priority sorts first in ascending order).

`votes`, `watches`: the counts; `description`, `environment`: the raw text; `duedate`, `resolutiondate`, `created`, `updated`: the Jira timestamps; `timespent`, `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`: the raw values in seconds (not milliseconds); `workratio`: Jira's work ratio of the issue (`WorkRatio.getWorkRatio`).

`assignee`, `creator`, `reporter`: the user's display name (C-0876); `project`: the project name; `components`: a `ComparableTuple` of the component names in the issue's order; `labels`: a tuple of the label texts; `fixVersions` and `versions` (affects versions): a tuple of the versions' sequences. An issue with no components, labels or versions gets the empty tuple (defined, sorting first).

`issue-time-field-provider` answers attribute ids `timespent` (time spent), `timeestimate` (remaining estimate) and `timeoriginalestimate` (original estimate) for issues, served in format `duration` whatever format was requested, with any params. The value is Jira's value in seconds multiplied by 1000 (milliseconds), e.g. 3600 s gives 3600000; a null value gives the undefined value. Every other id is declined; non-issue items get the undefined value.

`date-field-provider` answers `created`, `updated` and `resolutiondate` for issues in format `time` (whatever format was requested): the Jira timestamp in epoch milliseconds, no correction; a null date (e.g. unresolved) gives the undefined value.

`duedate` is a date-only field. With param `disableDateShift` = true the value is the due date's stored timestamp in epoch milliseconds, unchanged. Otherwise (param absent or false) the due date is corrected to the viewing user's time zone as `structure-datetime-formatter` does (C-1669: the calendar date in the JVM time zone, at 00:00 in the context's time zone), and the loader declares `USER_TIMEZONE`. No due date gives the undefined value. Every other id is declined.

`enum-customfield-order-provider` answers only attribute id `customfield` in format `order`, with param `fieldId` (long). It declines other ids, other formats, a missing or 0 `fieldId`, a field id Jira's `CustomFieldManager` does not know, and custom field types not listed in the next claim. Values are for issues only; an issue for which the field is not relevant (outside its configuration context) and an empty field give the undefined value.

Sort values by the Jira custom field type (checked in this order): single select: the option's sequence; multi select: the first selected option's sequence; cascading select: (parent sequence, child sequence) as a `ComparableTuple` when a child is chosen, (parent sequence, `Long.MIN_VALUE`) when only a parent is; labels: the first label's text; project picker: the project's name (looked up by id in `ProjectManager`); version picker: the first version as the tuple (project key, version sequence, version name); single user: the user's display name; ScriptRunner user-aware script field (type class `com.onresolve.scriptrunner.customfield.UserAwareScriptField`, only when ScriptRunner is installed): its user's display name; multi user: the first user's display name; multi group: the first group's name.

For a field whose type key starts with `com.coresoftlabs.secure-fields.secure-fields` (the Secure Fields app), the loader adds the `USER` context dependency, so values are computed per viewing user; other fields add none.
